message:
chore(release): 0.2.111 -- a version, so the in-app path can be driven once

One line: the version constant. No features, no refactoring, no unrelated fixes.
Android untouched at 0.2.16, and the 0.2.110 files and signature stay as they are.

The bootstrap is done -- the installed updater is 538,624 bytes / 0ac7aea8, the
fixed one, because the user installed 0.2.110 by hand. But 0.2.110 installed
against 0.2.110 published is is_newer=false, so nothing happens. Driving the
in-app path for real needs exactly one thing: a higher version.

Only the binaries that embed the version constant changed hash -- Host, Client,
Updater, Setup. Stream, Capture, InputService, Viewer and the two html files are
byte-identical to 0.2.110, which is fine: a new version directory, so the
immutability guard does not apply.

And the backup situation fixed itself as predicted: manifest-backups/0.2.110 holds
ten artifacts, so a bare-version name is a valid rollback point again. #510 said
that gate 7 would stop the broken shape recurring; this is the first backup where
it shows.

What is NOT verified is the point of the release. The in-app update has not been
run. The verdict comes from updater.log -- Req, Quiesce, ten-file Swap, Register,
RequiredHealth, Commit, Optional -- plus the installed version and the updater's
bytes. Not from anything on screen.
